data.name: Nicodemia
data.gender_notes: Nicodemia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Greek name Nikodemos, derived from nikos (victory) and demos (people). In the New Testament, Nicodemus was a Pharisee and a secret disciple of Jesus. The name Nicodemia carries the meaning “Victorious in battle” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Nicodemia usually hope their child will grow to embody victorious in battle and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes new beginnings and triumph over adversity.
data.etymology: Nicodemia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victorious in battle.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nicodemia total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_greek.name: Νικοδήμεια

in_latin.name: Nicodemia

in_english.name: Nicodemia
in_english.long_meaning: The name Nicodemia is derived from the Greek words nike and demos, meaning victory and people, and its significance is the victory of the people, used as a Christian name

data.cultural_impact: Nicodemus is known for his dual role in Christian history - as a Pharisee, representative of Jewish religious leadership, and as a Christian, one of the earliest recorded converts to Jesus' teachings. His name symbolizes the fluidity and complexity of religious identity, particularly in a multicultural society where individuals may hold multiple affiliations.
data.spiritual_significance: Nicodemus' name embodies the transformative power of spiritual growth and the journey towards true understanding. The name "Nicodemia" can serve as a reminder of the ongoing process of self-discovery and the importance of staying open to new experiences, insights, and perspectives. It further underscores the strength and courage required to challenge long-held beliefs and commit to a new path.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nicodemus, meaning "victory of the people of God," embodies the transformative power of divine grace in the life of a seeker. Nicodemia, as a female variant, symbolizes the triumphant spirit of a woman, who, guided by faith, navigates her life's journey towards spiritual rebirth and redemption.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that In the 4th century, Saint Nicodemia was a Christian martyr. The name Nicodemia carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: She was venerated in the Eastern Orthodox Church.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Nicodemia remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Sarah Nicodemia in Dublin, Ireland credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Nicodemia, which means "Victorious in battle". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
